result.summary: Executed docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-029.md against branch feature/WF02-REQ-029 at commit c37d535. Wrote the new committed test file apps/bot/src/handlers/checkinQr.forgery.test.ts (7 cases: AC1 cross-event-staff, AC2 xmin zero-write proof, AC3 single-row waitlisted/requested/withdrawn cycle with override-button assertion on all three, AC5 company:null branch, AC6 positive + AC6 negative cross-chapter organizer, and the S4 stale-token recheck's two-sub-case case: full-dispatch + direct performQrCheckIn call), per this project's established TEST-DESIGNER-designs/TEST-RUNNER-writes convention (matching REQ-028's identical framing). npm run lint: 0 errors (2 pre-existing apps/web /LCP warnings in Footer.tsx/Nav.tsx, unrelated to this change and its diff). npm run build: apps/web (Next.js 16.3.2, Turbopack) and apps/bot (tsc) both clean. npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism from the REPO ROOT (TEST_DATABASE_URL/DATABASE_URL against a freshly docker-composed + drizzle-kit-migrated scratch Postgres on port 55432): 29 test files / 293 tests passed, 0 failed -- up from the 286-test baseline by exactly the 7 new cases this run added. Re-ran the new file alone to confirm the count is real: 1 file / 7 tests passed. This is the authoritative, freshly-run repo-root count, never carried over from an earlier step's report. AC1 (independent, cross-event-staff fixture): Cross-Staff is real EventStaff of Event Y only, scans Event X's attendee's token. Reply===notStaff; exactly one audit_log row action=checkin.refused naming the attendee's registrationId (not either event's id), actorUserId=Cross-Staff; registrations row untouched (all three columns null) -- PASS. AC2 (independent, xmin storage-layer proof): first scan sets checkedInAt/checkInMethod=qr, one registration.checkin audit row. xmin captured immediately after first scan and again after a second scan of the SAME token: identical -- the row was never physically rewritten, a strictly stronger proof than value-unchanged. checkedInAt/checkedInBy/checkInMethod byte-for-byte unchanged, still exactly one audit row -- PASS. AC3 (independent, single-row 3-state cycle): one registration's admission column flipped waitlisted -> requested -> withdrawn in sequence (token preserved); on each of the 3 scans, reply text matches the exact per-admission catalog key AND reply_markup carries exactly one override button (callback_data/label both asserted) on all three iterations, not just one; checkedInAt stays null throughout -- PASS. AC5 (independent, company:null branch): attendee A (company populated) reply contains name+company, excludes phone/email, counter=1; attendee B (company: null) reply contains name, excludes phone/email, counter=2, and contains NO orphan ' -- ' separator anywhere -- PASS. AC6 positive (independent fixture): same-chapter organizer's override admits+checks in a withdrawn registration; registrations row admission=admitted/checkedInBy=organizer/checkInMethod=manual; exactly one registration.override_admit_checkin audit row; success reply contains name+company -- PASS. AC6 negative (independent, cross-chapter organizer fixture): a genuine organizer of Chapter Q (not a plain staff volunteer) taps Chapter P's event's override button; registrations row unchanged (still withdrawn, checkedInAt still null); zero override_admit_checkin audit rows; answerCallbackQuery show_alert=true, text===overrideNotAuthorized -- confirms requireOrganizerForChapter's chapter-scoping specifically, a distinct failure mode from BACKEND-DEV's own 'plain EventStaff, no organizer role anywhere' negative case -- PASS. Stale-token S4 sub-case A (full dispatch, user-facing behavior): fixture built from a GENUINE re-registration (admitted T1 -> withdrawn, T1 preserved, confirmed via direct SELECT -> re-registered on the same event, same registrationId R reused per REQ-022, new token T2 confirmed != T1 via direct SELECT). Dispatching /start ci_ (the OLD token) is refused as unknownToken at the unlocked-lookup stage, exactly as the spec's own reachability argument predicts (ordinary sequential dispatch can never reach performQrCheckIn's internal recheck) -- PASS. Stale-token S4 sub-case B (direct performQrCheckIn call, the defensive code path itself -- the one line with zero prior coverage anywhere in this codebase per SECURITY-REVIEWER/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own flag): performQrCheckIn(db, R, T1, staffUserId, now) called directly with the real registrationId paired with the now-stale T1. outcome.kind==='unknown-token' -- this is design §3.3 step 2's own recheck firing (row R genuinely exists; a plain id-based lookup would otherwise have found it and proceeded to decideQrCheckinOutcome). xmin identical before/after the call -- genuine zero-write proof, no UPDATE ran. Zero new registration.checkin audit rows for R -- PASS. This closes the zero-coverage gap the spec identified. AC7 (git grep, no vitest case per spec): git grep -i "web_app|webapp|mini.?app" apps/bot/src returns 11 hits, every one the pre-existing has_main_web_app: false field inside each *.test.ts file's FAKE_BOT_INFO fixture (a real grammY BotInfo field disabling that Telegram feature, identical convention already in 10 other pre-existing test files) -- not Mini App/WebApp/custom-client implementation code -- PASS. Full detail and real command output is in test-reports/report-2026-09-07-WF02-REQ-029.yaml.
